subject.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane

question: Should Active Memory allow one concurrent recall per agent, or must this PR also preserve a gateway-wide aggregate concurrency cap?
rationale: Both choices are technically viable, but they express different availability and resource-governance policy: per-agent lanes prevent cross-agent starvation while increasing worst-case aggregate recall load.

options.title: Accept per-agent lanes
options.body: Land one max-concurrency-one lane per agent and track aggregate fleet throttling separately if production evidence shows it is needed.

options.title: Require an aggregate cap
options.body: Keep agent-scoped fairness but add a process-level recall semaphore or equivalent owner-approved cap before merge.

recommendation.title: Accept per-agent lanes
recommendation.body: Land one max-concurrency-one lane per agent and track aggregate fleet throttling separately if production evidence shows it is needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the predecessor lane isolation after the same lane-scope tradeoff was explicitly surfaced in review.
